parts.title: A week without my phone
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When my mother told me that I could not use my phone for a week, I thought it was a terrible joke. I am fifteen, and I use my phone for everything: talking to friends, listening to music, and even waking up in the morning.

On the first day, I kept reaching for my pocket every few minutes. By the evening, I felt strangely lost. I did not know what was happening in my friends' lives, and I imagined that everyone was talking about me. I almost gave up.

But on the third day, something changed. I read an entire book for the first time in months, and I went for a long walk with my dog without checking any messages. At dinner, my parents and I talked for an hour about nothing in particular, and I realised how much I had missed it.

When the week ended, I was surprised that I did not run to my phone. I switched it on, answered the important messages, and then left it on the kitchen table. I still use it every day, but now I turn it off at ten o'clock, and I sleep much better.

He thought it was a joke

questions.explanation: He thought it was a terrible joke.

questions.explanation: By the evening he felt strangely lost and imagined that everyone was talking about him.

questions.explanation: He read a whole book and went for a long walk with his dog.

parts.title: How to stay safe online
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Millions of teenagers use social media every day, and most of them have a great time. [1] However, there are a few simple rules that can help you avoid problems.

First, choose strong passwords. A good password has at least twelve letters and includes numbers. [2] Never use the same password for different accounts, because if one is stolen, all the others are in danger.

Second, think carefully before you share a photograph. [3] Once a picture is online, you cannot control who sees it or where it goes. Ask yourself whether you would be happy for your teacher or your grandmother to look at it.

Third, be careful about meeting people that you only know online. [4] If you do decide to meet someone, take a friend with you and choose a public place. Finally, remember that you can always talk to an adult if something makes you feel uncomfortable. [5] They will not be angry, and they might be able to help.
sentences: Photos can stay on the internet for years.
Many adults forget their passwords too.
The internet can be a wonderful place to make friends and learn new things.
Not everyone is honest about who they are.
Using your pet's name is not a good idea.
Parents and teachers usually understand more than you expect.
Ask a teacher to show you how to report a problem.
Some websites ask you to give your date of birth.

gaps.explanation: "Have a great time" is followed by the positive description, and "However" introduces the rules.
A good password is described, and a pet's name is an example of what to avoid.
"Once a picture is online" explains why photos stay on the internet for a long time.
Not everyone is honest explains why meeting online friends is risky.
"They" refers to parents and teachers, who will not be angry.

parts.title: The school computer club
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: ellery
turns.text: Welcome to our Computer Club, everyone. My name is Mr Ellery, and I’ll be your teacher. First, when we meet. The club used to be on Tuesdays, but the room is being painted, so from this term we meet every Thursday after school. We start at four o’clock and we finish at half past five. Some of you asked me if we could stay until six, but the school bus leaves at a quarter to six, so that’s not possible. Now, what are we going to do? Many of you hope to make a computer game, and we may do a little of that at the end of the year, but this term we are going to learn how to build a website. By December, each of you will have your own. You will need a USB stick to keep your work. You can buy one in the school shop for three pounds. Last year they cost five pounds, but the shop found a cheaper supplier. If you already have an old one at home, that’s fine, as long as it has enough space. Next, safety. I’ll teach you a lot about this, but let me start with passwords. Many people think eight characters are enough. It used to be true, but now experts say you need at least ten characters, with numbers and letters. Please don’t use your name or your birthday. Finally, how many of us can there be? The room has twenty computers, but we need space to move around, and I can’t help more than fifteen students at a time. So there are fifteen places, and so far twelve students have signed up. If you have friends who want to join, tell them to see me by Friday. That’s all. Any questions?

gaps.explanation: Mr Ellery says it used to be Tuesdays, but now it meets every Thursday.

gaps.explanation: They may do a game later in the year, but this term they learn to build a website.

parts.title: A teenage video-maker
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: concetta
turns.text: Kasimir, you’re sixteen and you make videos. What were your first ones about?

turns.speaker: kasimir
turns.text: Well, I thought I’d make cooking videos, because my mum is a great cook. I filmed two, but they were boring, mostly me cutting onions. A friend suggested music and dance, and we tried one, but it was a disaster. Then I filmed my friends skateboarding in the park, and it felt right. People started watching, and I haven’t stopped since.

turns.speaker: concetta
turns.text: How many followers do you have?

turns.speaker: kasimir
turns.text: A lot of people think it’s twenty thousand, because my best video has that many views. But that’s just one video. Last year I had about two hundred followers, and now it’s about two thousand. It isn’t huge, but I’m really happy with it, because most of those people write to me and I know their names.

turns.speaker: concetta
turns.text: How do you feel about unkind comments?

turns.speaker: kasimir
turns.text: Honestly, they don’t really bother me now. I used to answer them, and that only made it worse. I thought about deleting a video once, but it seemed silly to let one person decide. These days I just don’t read them, and I tell my friends to do the same when they start filming. My brother says I’m too calm, but it works for me.

turns.speaker: concetta
turns.text: What’s your most important safety rule?

turns.speaker: kasimir
turns.text: My real name is on the channel, and my parents agreed to that, so it isn’t the rule. Filming in public is hard to avoid, because skateboarding happens outside. The rule I never break is that I don’t show where I live, so no street signs and no house number in the background. I check each video twice before I post it, and my dad checks it once more.

turns.speaker: concetta
turns.text: When do you make them?

turns.speaker: kasimir
turns.text: I’m too tired after school to film in the evenings. The holidays are great because I have more time, but I can’t wait three months for the next video. So I film on Saturday with my friends, and I edit on Sunday afternoon. That’s my routine, and I keep to it, even when it rains and the park is empty.

turns.speaker: concetta
turns.text: Why do you want to study film-making?

turns.speaker: kasimir
turns.text: I thought about computer science, because I like editing on the computer, and my teacher says I’m good at music, because I make my own soundtracks. But what I love most is telling a story with pictures. A film can make people laugh or cry, and that’s what I want to do. That’s why I’d like to go to film school.

parts.title: Getting to know you
parts.instructions: Answer each question in your own words. Aim to speak for 20-30 seconds.

questions.prompt: How often do you use your phone? What do you use it for?
Do you use social media? Which sites or apps do you like?
Tell me about a time when the internet was very useful to you.
Would you like to live without technology for a week? Why or why not?

parts.instructions: Look at the photograph and speak for about one minute. Describe what you can see and say what the person might be feeling.
